rounds.text: B & A Ltd presents a compelling value proposition as it trades at a significant discount to its book value with a P/B of 0.88x [E2, E56], which is less than half the sector benchmark of 1.83x [E7]. While historical growth has been slow, the business is undergoing a sharp operational turnaround, evidenced by a 212% year-over-year increase in net profit [E63] and a 29% surge in sales [E61, E62]. This recovery is further supported by quarterly operating margins expanding by 9 percentage points to reach 9% in June 2026 [E28], contributing to a perfect results score of 100/100 [E68]. Despite this momentum, the company’s EV/EBITDA of 8.59x remains well below the sector median of 11.58x [E11], while the share price sits at just 29% of its 52-week range [E5]. Conceded: the company currently reports a negative return on equity of -2.9% [E13, E65], a high P/E of 163x [E1], and negative free cash flow of Rs -25 Cr [E33]. With promoters increasing their stake [E39] and trailing twelve-month sales growth accelerating to 11% [E17], the current market price appears to be overlooking a fundamental shift in the company's earnings trajectory [E68].
